final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more precise: aggregate readiness, rollback, and monitoring support deployment prudence, while policy still requires disclosure for a material limitation in a named launch use case unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. But the key compliance predicate remains unmet in the evidence available to this role. The record still shows an exposed below-target health-plan benefits support segment, an unsigned risk-acceptance draft that does not cover that exposure, and no proof that the required model-card disclosure was actually completed before launch. That means the Actor's narrowed position may describe a potentially compliant path, but it does not establish that the path has been satisfied. This is enough to avoid a harsher noncompliance conclusion, but not enough to move to compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat here is itself an unresolved pre-launch requirement rather than a mere disclosure note attached to an otherwise completed compliance showing.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows the health-plan benefits support use case is below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is still no approved risk acceptance that addresses the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
There is still no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch model-card disclosure has been completed or approved.
The recommended action remains overbroad unless certification is expressly conditioned on completed disclosure; agreement that disclosure is needed does not satisfy the policy predicate by itself.
